notes:
The San Francisco Civic Center historic district nomination (1978), read whole. It is the document the previous batch fetched and left: it is in neither the NPS index's city query nor its county query, and the previous run found it only by knowing the listing exists.

A district nomination is a different shape from a single-building one. There is no SPECIFIC DATES field to read; the payload is section 7, which walks the district building by building with a date in the heading and a street number in the first line of each, and section 8, which gives the architect and the construction years in prose. Eleven buildings and structures are described and ten of them carry a street number. City Hall does not — the nomination locates it by the block it occupies and never prints a number for it — so no finding is written for it here.

The architects' biographies at the end of section 8 credit six practitioners across the district, and those credits are attached to the buildings the same section names, not inferred from the biography alone.

coverage.remaining: 111 listings certified 1980 or later are unread, of which the 42 certified 1980-1989 are read in the sibling batch listed-1980-1989. After those: 1990-1999 (17), 2000-2009 (22), 2010-2015 (15) and 2016-2023 (15), plus 77000334 (Mills Building and Tower), whose PDF has no text layer.
coverage.note: Read one district nomination of 99,288 characters. Ten of the eleven buildings and structures it describes carry a street number; City Hall is the one that does not. 17 findings out of the ten addressed buildings — construction dates for eight of them, four dated alterations, and two dated events of national record.

findings.description: Built as the War Memorial Opera House to the design of Arthur Brown, Jr., with G. Albert Lansburgh assisting. Steel frame with reinforced concrete floors and walls, clad in terra cotta simulating granite, four principal storeys under a leaded copper mansard roof.

citation.label: National Register of Historic Places nomination, San Francisco Civic Center (reference number 78000757), National Park Service.
citation.locator: section 7, Description; section 8, Statement of Significance

raw.text: the Opera House (309 Van Ness Avenue) ... Construction finally began in the summer of 1931 and was complete in the fall of 1932 ... G. Albert Lansburgh, who assisted Arthur Brown with the Opera House

resolution.method: The nomination's numbers — 309 and 459 Van Ness Avenue — are in sf-eas-addresses at neither number. It identifies the buildings by name and by the double block they occupy, bounded by Van Ness, McAllister, Franklin and Grove Streets, and EAS puts 301 VAN NESS AVE (the Opera House) and 401 VAN NESS AVE (the Veterans Building) on one parcel, 0786A001, whose sf-parcels range is 301-401 VAN NESS AVE and which the assessor files as '0401 0301 VAN NESS AV'. One parcel is one page, at the lowest number.

publish.note: The page already dates the Opera House to 1932 and credits Arthur Brown Jr.
